body: The Scoring section says pairwise beats scoring in isolation but never mentions position bias (left/right order effects) in pairwise judging. Add what the corpus says about it and how to control for it, with cites.
reason: The corpus supports the request in detail. Stanford CME295 names position bias and the swap-and-majority remedy (8fNP4N46RRo@23, @24); the Northeastern lecture gives the 'always favors the first or the second' framing and training-time shuffling (N_DwZR--XCc@46); the RAG-metrics talk gives randomised order and allowing ties as pairwise best practice (cRz0BWkuwHg@6); and the evals playbook gives the paired swap test, the 'neither answer has demonstrated superiority' reading of a flip, the aggregate-or-report-reversals production rule and anonymised pairs (PjCwlX0XT8o@36, @37, @32). Added as a new lever card directly after the pairwise card, with a cited pointer sentence in the pairwise card itself so the correction lands where the reader was reading.
